title: La psychanalyse de Dom Juan  (The Psychoanalysis of Dom Juan)

segments.t: The following morning, Colette arrives at the theatre rehearsal hall to return Andrea's apartment keys and personal belongings. Watching Christophe Bel direct Francois Berleand on stage, Colette cannot help offering her own clinical interpretation of Moliere's legendary character. Fascinated by her insights, the pretentious young director hangs on her every word. Listen to the scene in French first. Don't worry about catching every word.
Refuser de nager, c'est refuser la norme!
La soif de vivre de Dom Juan est là.
Tout est permis, sauf la norme de la monogamie.
Il a tellement peur de cette norme.
Il se réfugie avec tout ce qui porte une jupe.
Ce n'est pas son désir qui l'empêche d'être fidèle.
C'est sa peur!
Pardon? Vous pouvez répéter?
Sur la peur de la norme?
Je vais vous donner mon livre.
Vous comprendrez.
Je vais le dédicacer.
Le Donjuanisme ou La Maladie du Lien.
J'y mets mon numéro de téléphone aussi?
Non. La dédicace suffit.
Juste la dédicace?
Bravo! Bravo, le directeur!
Let's walk through it as Colette shares her sharp psychological critique step by step.
Refuser de nager, c'est refuser la norme!
'Refusing to swim is refusing the norm!' An infinitive verb can serve directly as a sentence subject.
La soif de vivre de Dom Juan est là.
'Dom Juan\'s thirst for life is right there.' The adverb 'there' points out the core of his personality.
Tout est permis, sauf la norme de la monogamie.
'Everything is allowed, except the norm of monogamy.' The preposition 'except' marks an exception.
Il a tellement peur de cette norme.
'He is so afraid of this norm.' The idiom 'has' expresses fear of something.
Il se réfugie avec tout ce qui porte une jupe.
'He takes refuge with anything wearing a skirt.' The relative pronoun 'that' serves as subject of the clause.
Ce n'est pas son désir qui l'empêche d'être fidèle.
'It isn't his desire that stops him being faithful.' The construction 'empecher de' means 'to prevent from'.
C'est sa peur!
'It\'s his fear!' The demonstrative 'c\'est' puts sharp rhetorical focus on fear.
Pardon? Vous pouvez répéter?
'Pardon? Can you repeat that?' The modal 'can' asks a polite request.
Sur la peur de la norme?
'About the fear of the norm?' The preposition 'about' indicates the topic in question.
Je vais vous donner mon livre.
'I am going to give you my book.' The near future uses 'am going to' plus infinitive.
Vous comprendrez.
'You will understand.' The simple future 'will understand' promises future clarity.
Je vais le dédicacer.
'I am going to sign it.' The direct object pronoun 'it' precedes the infinitive.
Le Donjuanisme ou La Maladie du Lien.
'Donjuanism or The Sickness of the Bond.' Colette recites the formal title of her book.
J'y mets mon numéro de téléphone aussi?
'Shall I put my phone number too?' The pronoun 'y' refers back to inside the book.
Non. La dédicace suffit.
'No. The dedication is enough.' The verb 'suffices' firmly declines Christophe's advance.
Juste la dédicace?
'Just the dedication?' The adverb 'just' expresses mild disappointment.
Bravo! Bravo, le directeur!
'Bravo! Well done, director!' Francois mocks the young director from the stage. Now listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.

Colette gave Christophe the artistic inspiration he needed, while keeping him firmly at arm's length.
